clue.text: Question the capacity of part of the hydro

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently for information
room means space or capacity, as in 'room for six'

explanation.surface: Someone queries how much a section of a spa hotel can hold.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a British spa hotel offering hydropathic treatment; its chamber where visitors drink the waters has a traditional name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spa hotels had a hall where mineral water was dispensed to visitors, a standard feature of such establishments.

clue.text: Suffer to travel on the Tube?

definitions.meaning: to suffer something is to endure or experience it
read whimsically as 'go under', travelling beneath the streets on London's Underground

explanation.definitionFit: Enduring an ordeal is going through it, and riding London's Tube is literally going below ground.

clue.text: Ancient painter

definitions.meaning: ancient in the sense of early, belonging to the earliest stage
an untrained or pre-Renaissance artist working in a naive style

explanation.definitionFit: The word means belonging to an early stage of development, and also names an artist of naive or pre-Renaissance style.

clue.text: Musical performances during work periods

parts.note: op. is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work
eras are periods of history

explanation.surface: Concerts are being staged during office hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Staged dramatic works set to music are among the grandest forms of musical performance.

clue.text: Changes — so many during the present time for families

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the next words are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A reflection on how much shifts for families in the modern era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' is the anagram signal working on SO MANY DURING THE, fifteen letters. 'Present' reads as 'current' but refers to a gift: a day when families give their mother presents.
explanation.definitionFit: This British spring festival, the fourth Sunday of Lent, is when children give gifts and cards to their mothers.

clue.text: River man was unruly

parts.note: rio is the Spanish and Portuguese word for a river, familiar from Rio Grande
Ted is a common man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man by the river behaved badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving riotously means being disorderly, the conduct of an unruly crowd.

clue.text: Money in trust not long ago

indicators.note: in tells us one word's letters are placed inside another's

parts.note: to rely on someone is to trust them
a cent is a small coin, standing for money

explanation.surface: Someone recently put cash into a trust fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening lately happened only a short while back.

clue.text: The right leaders on US island to give support for climbers

indicators.note: leaders here means the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: Ellis Island in New York harbour was the main US immigration station

explanation.surface: Instructions about putting up a frame on an American island.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice frame lets climbing plants such as roses grow up a wall.

clue.text: Ship takes animals out of southern city

indicators.note: the animals stand outside, so their letters wrap round the southern city

parts.note: deer are animals (the plural is the same as the singular)
Troy is the ancient city besieged by the Greeks

explanation.surface: A vessel carrying animals away from a city in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast warship built to escort fleets and attack submarines is a type of naval ship.

clue.text: Bad dream about one to idolise

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the one
bad here means the letters of the following word are spoiled, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Having a nightmare about the person you worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges DREAM as ADMRE, and 'about' puts I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to regard them with great approval and respect.

clue.text: Lacking diplomacy, didn't secure so much, so they say

indicators.note: so they say means the words before are heard, not seen

parts.note: tacked less means fastened with fewer tacks

explanation.surface: A clumsy diplomat failed to win as much as hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacked less' (secured with fewer tacks) is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without diplomacy is insensitive, blundering where others take care.

clue.text: Angry about swindle in water

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes round the swindle

parts.note: irate means angry
to rig is to fix dishonestly, a swindle

explanation.surface: Someone furious about being cheated while in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like a noun (where the swindle happened) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply land with channels of liquid for crops is to water it.

clue.text: Racehorse fixer loses heart — becomes more honourable

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a nobbler drugs or tampers with a racehorse to stop it winning, a British term

explanation.surface: A crooked racing man grows a conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses heart' drops the middle B of NOBBLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning high-minded, of fine character.

clue.text: Put the highest-ranking in charge of the subject

parts.note: top means highest-ranking, as in the top brass

explanation.surface: Instructions to make the most senior person responsible for the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme under discussion is the subject of a talk or essay.

clue.text: Studied writer of farce on newspaper boss

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the famous Aldwych farces of the 1920s
ed is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A comic playwright is put above a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers was an English playwright of farces such as Rookery Nook.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over a subject carefully, examining it thoroughly, is an older sense of the verb meaning to cross.

clue.text: "I shot an arrow into the air" — how did I do it?

definitions.text: "I shot an arrow into the air" — how did I do it?

parts.words: "I shot an arrow into the air" — how did I do it?
parts.note: Longfellow's poem continues 'It fell to earth, I knew not where', so the shot was fired with no target in mind

explanation.surface: A line from a poem followed by a question about the archer's technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting without aiming at anything means acting without a goal or direction.

clue.text: Cars meant, perhaps, to be ceremonial

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Vehicles intended for a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges CARS and MEANT. 'Ceremonial' is used as a noun, a rite.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious rite such as baptism or communion is a solemn ceremony.

clue.text: Admirer of girl sporting a dimple

indicators.note: sporting means displaying or wearing, so one part carries the other within it

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow, like a dimple
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone smitten by a girl with a dimple.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of someone is devoted to them.

clue.text: A very quiet finish — time for something extra

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
end means finish
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A hushed ending, then a moment for an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: An attached part or addition that is subsidiary to the main thing.

clue.text: Grazing land beyond the river

parts.note: past means beyond, as in 'past the church'
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Fields for livestock across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadow where cattle and sheep feed on grass.

clue.text: Here in Paris the king is more glacial

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: A French monarch is even colder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning covered in frost or very cold.

clue.text: Isle of stone?

parts.note: Ireland's poetic nickname shares its name with a green gem

explanation.definitionFit: A green precious gem gives Ireland its nickname, celebrating the island's greenery.

clue.text: Measure that helps to create concealed lighting

definitions.meaning: a measure of capacity for grain, eight gallons

definitions.text: that helps to create concealed lighting
definitions.meaning: from the saying about hiding your light under one, keeping talents modest

explanation.definitionFit: It is a dry measure for grain, and the vessel in the biblical saying under which a light is hidden.

clue.text: Quarters for an old Jewish communist

parts.note: the quarters of the compass are its points: east, south, south, east, north, east
the quarters of the compass are its points: east, south, south, east, north, east
the quarters of the compass are its points: east, south, south, east, north, east
the quarters of the compass are its points: east, south, south, east, north, east
the quarters of the compass are its points: east, south, south, east, north, east
the quarters of the compass are its points: east, south, south, east, north, east

explanation.surface: Living space found for an ancient Jewish revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like lodgings but means compass points, here six of them in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an ascetic sect in ancient Judea held property in common, living communally.

clue.text: Howled when girl came back with a boy

indicators.note: came back means the girl's name is written backwards

parts.note: Lulu is a girl's name, also the Scottish singer
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Wailing broke out when a girl returned with a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came back' turns LULU round to ULUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wailed loudly, as mourners or wolves do.

clue.text: Test depth round the resort

indicators.note: round means the depth test goes around the next word

parts.note: to sound water is to measure its depth

explanation.surface: Measuring the water off a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHEND (Southend-on-Sea) is an Essex seaside resort near London.
explanation.definitionFit: This Essex town on the Thames estuary is a classic British seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: Hen, say, torn apart by these animals

indicators.note: torn apart says the letters of the words are pulled about

explanation.surface: A chicken savaged by scavengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing scavenging carnivores of Africa are the beasts meant.

clue.text: "Than are — of in your philosophy" (Hamlet)

parts.note: Hamlet tells Horatio there are more things in heaven and earth than his philosophy has imagined; fill the blank

explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing word means imagined or conceived of in sleep.

clue.text: It sounds as if you will get drawn to the festival

indicators.note: it sounds as if means the following words are heard rather than read

parts.note: you'll plus tied, drawn as in a game ending level

explanation.surface: A promise that you will be attracted to the celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' means tied, a level result, not attracted; YOU'LL plus TIED is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for the Christmas season, the midwinter festival.
